name: Non-syndromic Unisutural Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal skull shape consistent with premature fusion of a single cranial suture
Imaging evidence (CT or X-ray) confirming premature fusion of one cranial suture without involvement of other sutures
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic craniosynostosis or associated systemic anomalies
Normal neurodevelopmental milestones in early infancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Abnormal skull shape with radiological confirmation of single suture fusion and exclusion of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, radiological, and genetic assessment to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Premature fusion of a single cranial suture
pathognomonic.notes: Typically sagittal, coronal, or metopic suture involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal skull shape corresponding to fused suture
pathognomonic.notes: Includes scaphocephaly, plagiocephaly, or trigonocephaly depending on suture
searchTerms: skull shape abnormal from fused suture
unusual head shape due to suture fusion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable ridging over affected cranial suture
pathognomonic.notes: Firm bony ridge along fused suture line
searchTerms: ridge felt on closed cranial suture

common.notes: Prominent forehead due to compensatory growth
Uneven skull contour related to suture fusion
May be observed in some cases
searchTerms: delayed closing of soft spot on head

occasional.notes: Headache, irritability, vomiting in some cases
searchTerms: headache and vomiting from brain swelling

occasional.notes: Misalignment of eyes due to orbital asymmetry
Conductive hearing loss secondary to cranial deformity
Mild facial distortion related to skull shape

rare.symptomName: Visual impairment due to optic nerve compression
searchTerms: vision loss from optic nerve pressure
blurred vision due to nerve compression

imaging: CT scan showing premature fusion of a single cranial suture
Skull X-ray demonstrating suture obliteration and abnormal skull morphology
genetic: Absence of mutations associated with syndromic craniosynostosis genes (e.g., FGFR2, TWIST1)
other: Clinical examination revealing palpable suture ridging and abnormal head shape

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic anomalies (e.g., limb abnormalities, developmental delay)
Positive genetic mutations in syndromic genes
Molding deformity due to external pressure

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (vomiting, irritability, bulging fontanelle)
Multiple suture involvement or systemic abnormalities suggestive of syndromic craniosynostosis
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: diagnosis, evaluation, and management. 2000.
Wilkie AO, Johnson D, Wall SA. Clinical genetics of craniosynostosis. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2017.
